claims_disputed.claim: Skills are most useful when construction depends on implicit procedural knowledge
claims_disputed.reason: Table 3 caption: tasks are 'grouped according to the mechanisms discussed in RQ3', i.e. the 'procedural-knowledge-dependent' group (1a/1b/3b) is defined by where Skills helped; no independent, a-priori measure of implicit procedural knowledge exists, so the conditional is circular. The measured fact (18/30 -> 29/30 on three QA tasks) is solid; the attribution to a task property is not. The 4a/4b 'despite correct DAG generation' diagnosis (§4.5) is asserted without failure-analysis data.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: Table 1: MCP-only (registry + state via MCP) loses 10.9 pp pass rate vs Context-Aware CC (83.3 vs 94.2) while cutting cost ($0.321 vs $0.456); reliability is recovered only once Skills are added. The MCP arm also changes the action space (DAG vs scripts, §4.1 'rather than an isolated difference'), so MCP is not isolated. The review's own note and applicability text describe this trade-off; the tag should match.
The paper reports tokens/cost/latency per configuration (Table 1) but implements and tests no token or cost budget or cap; reporting cost is not the pattern.

MCP-only vs DataFlow-Harness is a single-factor ablation (§4.1 settings 3 vs 4) and Skills win: 100/120 -> 112/120 runs (Table 1/3), Textbook-to-VQA precision 0.784 -> 0.972 and coverage 0.621 -> 0.873 (Table 2), and total tokens -25.5% (§4.3). The only reversal is 2b at 10/10 -> 9/10 (one run). Caveat: on-demand/progressive loading itself is not isolated; the comparison is skill content vs none.

P37 is a planner emitting subtask dependencies for (parallel) agent execution. Here a single Claude Code agent issues incremental mutations to a data-pipeline DAG that is the deliverable (§3.1, §3.3); there is no agent task plan and no parallel subtask execution. The review's own retag note concedes 'The DAG is the product artifact, not the agent's own subtask plan'. The DAG-vs-script comparison is also confounded with MCP grounding and action space (§4.1).

missed_issues: Table 1 cost column cannot be reconciled with the token column: Vanilla CC uses fewer input tokens than Context-Aware CC (153,584 vs 185,626) and only ~1.3K more output tokens, yet costs 2.1x ($0.950 vs $0.456). No linear list-price schedule reproduces both rows (solving gives ~$0.16/M input vs ~$374/M output), so the 72.5% and 42.8% cost figures depend on undisclosed caching/accounting. The review's 'Arithmetic checks out' covers only the percentages. The direction vs Context-Aware is still robust from tokens (~59% fewer total tokens) and latency.

Table 4 is worse for the harness than the review states. Vanilla CC wins MATH, Olympiad, Gaokao24_mix and Minerva at both epochs (GSM8K is split: the harness wins at 1 epoch). At 1 epoch the harness-trained model scores below the untrained base on MATH (72.3 vs 73.5) and Gaokao (38.5 vs 42.9), and at 2 epochs below base on Minerva (25.7 vs 26.5). The average gain comes from AIME24/25 and AMC23, which §4.6 itself calls the 'most contamination-sensitive' benchmarks. The seed pool is not described and synthesized data gets no decontamination check, so contamination is an unexamined alternative explanation.

Efficiency metrics are 'averaged over the same runs' (all 120, including failures), while latency is defined as time to 'a valid workflow artifact' (§4.1); the paper does not say how failed runs enter the latency and cost means.

Table 2 uses the protocol and metrics of FlipVQA-Miner [24], which comes from the same authors (Wong, Liang, He, Shen, Zhang). This adds to the self-evaluation already noted for the 12-task benchmark.

P33 is untagged. The central RQ1/RQ2 comparison is code-as-action (free-form Python scripts) vs typed MCP tool mutations. The result is mixed: scripts with codebase context have the highest pass rate (94.2) at 1.75x the harness cost.

Relevance note: the Textbook-to-VQA task (textbooks, interleaved solution manuals, exam sheets; §4.4) is the closest analogue to the team's education-cross-repository work. However, it is a single run with an unspecified annotation protocol.

The full operator registry and pipeline state are injected before every turn (§3.2), the opposite of deferred tool loading (P03). The token savings therefore come from the smaller action and output space, not from catalog trimming.
note: Same verdict and broadly accurate prose. However, the stance tags contradict the review's own notes: MCP-only lost about 11 pp, so P04 is mixed, not supports; cost reporting is not P24 budgets; and P37 does not apply to a deliverable DAG. The clean Skills ablation, meanwhile, earns P02 supports. The review also overstates cost reproducibility and understates how much Table 4 relies on contamination-sensitive AIME/AMC gains while other math scores fall below the base model.
